raw_case_text: A 34 year-old Thai man from Prajin Buri, a province in rural East Thailand, presented with a 4-month history of low-grade fever and multiple discrete painful umbilicated erythematous papules on his face, as well as a 40 kg weight loss from his previous normal weight of 110 kg and height of 170 cm. Two weeks prior to admission (PTA), he developed odynophagia, painful nodular ulcers on his tongue, and hoarseness of his voice. One week PTA, he had dyspnea on exertion. His medical history was unremarkable, and he denied using any pills, herbs, or intravenous drugs. His occupation was that of a car mechanic. He mentioned that he had not traveled to other locations in the previous three months. Physical examination revealed blood pressure of 90/50 mmHg, regular heart rate of 110/min, respiratory rate of 24/min, and body temperature of 38.3 C, mildly pale conjunctivae, multiple papules with central necrosis on his face painful nodular ulcers on his tongue and palate, diffuse fine crackles in both lungs, jugular vein engorgement, a positive left ventricular heave and a grade III/VI diastolic rumbling murmur at mitral valve area, hepatosplenomegaly, and mild pedal edema. The complete blood count (CBC) analysis showed a Hb of 11.1 g/dL, white blood cell of 5,350 x 103/muL, and platelets of 140,000/muL. Blood chemistries showed urea nitrogen of 56 mg/dL, creatinine of 1.98 mg/dL, total bilirubin of 4.9 mg/dL, direct bilirubin of 3.09 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase of 42 U/L, alanine aminotransferase of 25 U/L, alkaline phosphatase of 147 U/L, albumin of 3.1 g/dL, corrected calcium of 13.4 mg/dL, phosphorus of 3.1 mg/dL, intact parathyroid hormone of <1.2 (normal: 15-65) pmol/L, and 1,25-OH2 vitamin D of 152 (normal: 19.9-79.3) pg/mL. Anti-HIV serology testing showed negative results. Cardiomegaly with pulmonary congestion was seen on chest radiography. Transthoracic echocardiography indicated a left ventricular ejection fraction of 54%, moderate aortic regurgitation, severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, and multiple oscillating masses on the anterior mitral valve leaflet ranging from 1.5 cm to 2.4 cm in diameter (Figure 1(a), yellow arrows). Skin scraping of the facial lesion exhibited both extracellular and intracellular yeast-like organisms with buddings, 2-4 mum in size, on Wright's stain, most likely Histoplasma. As a result, disseminated histoplasmosis and endocarditis were diagnosed, and 3 mg/kg/day intravenous liposomal amphotericin B was administered immediately. The patient had a profound cardiogenic shock and atrial fibrillation one day after being admitted to the hospital, and echocardiography indicated a mechanical obstruction of the mitral valve orifice caused by the vegetation. Three large vegetations on the anterior mitral valve leaflet were identified during emergency open-heart surgery (Figure 1(b)), and a mechanical prosthetic mitral valve was placed. Histopathology examination of the vegetation showed many yeast-like organisms. However, the patient's condition deteriorated, and he died four days after the operation from intractable multiorgan failure. The sputum and vegetation cultures grew H. capsulatum (Figures 2(a) and 2(b)) after 1 week of incubation.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 34-year-old Thai male car mechanic from Prachin Buri Province presented with a 4-month history of low-grade fever, a 40 kg weight loss, and multiple painful umbilicated facial papules, a 2-week history of odynophagia, painful lingual ulcers, and hoarseness, and a 1-week history of exertional dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 4 months preceding admission, the previously healthy patient lost 40 kg (from a baseline weight of 110 kg at height 170 cm) and developed low-grade fevers and multiple painful umbilicated erythematous papules over his face. Two weeks before admission he developed painful nodular tongue/palatal ulcers, odynophagia, and hoarseness, followed 1 week before admission by exertional dyspnea.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable past medical history; denied prescription medications, herbal remedies, intravenous drug use, or recent travel outside Prachin Buri Province.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 4-month low-grade fever, 40 kg weight loss, painful facial papules, painful tongue/palate ulcers, odynophagia, hoarseness, and exertional dyspnea.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: blood pressure 90/50 mmHg, regular heart rate 110 beats/min, respiratory rate 24 breaths/min, and temperature 38.3 °C. Mucocutaneous exam showed mildly pale conjunctivae, multiple centrally necrotic/umbilicated erythematous papules on the face, and painful nodular ulcers on the tongue and palate. Cardiopulmonary and abdominal exam revealed jugular venous distension, a left ventricular heave, a grade III/VI diastolic rumbling murmur at the mitral area, diffuse bilateral fine pulmonary crackles, hepatosplenomegaly, and mild pedal edema.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC showed hemoglobin 11.1 g/dL, WBC 5,350/µL, and platelets 140,000/µL. Serum chemistry revealed azotemia (BUN 56 mg/dL, creatinine 1.98 mg/dL), cholestatic hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 4.9 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 3.09 mg/dL, AST 42 U/L, ALT 25 U/L, ALP 147 U/L, albumin 3.1 g/dL), and calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia: corrected calcium 13.4 mg/dL, phosphorus 3.1 mg/dL, suppressed intact PTH <1.2 pmol/L (normal 15–65), and markedly elevated 1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D of 152 pg/mL (normal 19.9–79.3). Anti-HIV serology was negative. Wright stain of a facial skin scraping showed 2–4 µm intracellular and extracellular budding yeast cells. Chest X-ray showed cardiomegaly and pulmonary edema.
objective.advanced_workup: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) demonstrated LVEF 54%, moderate aortic regurgitation, severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, and multiple large oscillating vegetations (1.5–2.4 cm) on the anterior mitral valve leaflet that acutely obstructed the mitral valve orifice on hospital day 2. Emergency open-heart mitral valve replacement excised three large anterior mitral leaflet vegetations; histopathology revealed abundant yeast-like organisms, and cultures of both the excised mitral vegetations and sputum grew Histoplasma capsulatum after 1 week.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Disseminated Histoplasma capsulatum infection (mucocutaneous lesions, granulomatous calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia [calcium 13.4 mg/dL, 1,25-(OH)2D 152 pg/mL], and hepatosplenomegaly) complicated by obstructive native-valve Histoplasma capsulatum mitral endocarditis (1.5–2.4 cm vegetations superimposed on severe rheumatic mitral stenosis) in an HIV-negative 34-year-old Thai man. Confirmed by Wright-stained facial skin scraping, mitral vegetation histopathology, and isolation of H. capsulatum from sputum and mitral valve vegetation cultures. Despite immediate intravenous liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day) and emergency mechanical mitral valve replacement for acute mitral orifice obstruction and cardiogenic shock on hospital day 2, the patient died on postoperative day 4 of refractory multiorgan failure.
